newsitem.title: UK: Newly structured Clearing House finds wide support.
newsitem.headline: Newly structured Clearing House finds wide support.

text.p: Only a few firms representing a tiny 1.65 percent of business have failed to take up shares in the newly structured London Clearing House (LCH), chief executive David Hardy said.
"We couldn't have hoped for a better result," said Hardy. LCH had set a minimum subscription level of 80 member firms representing 75 percent of clearing activity.
The new structure comes into force on Thursday October 10 with shares held by London's three derivative exchanges and 126 of the 174 members of the former clearing house.
Hardy said another three firms are joining but their formal share applications failed to arrive by last Friday's deadline.
Since 1982 the LCH has been owned by six British clearing banks.
Past mergers between companies account for 12 of the apparent decline in membership of the LCH and Hardy said this mainly represented large firms which had accumulated multiple memberships.
Under its new structure the LCH will have share capital of 50 million sterling with shares costing members 297,600 stg each.

These firms will subscribe to an additional default fund of 150 million stg divided between prorata with their trading volume and open interest with a minimum payment of 100,000 stg each. Cleared volume will represent 25 percent of this fund with the remainder pro rata to margins held at the LCH.

Hardy said the LCH now holds some 3.5 billion stg as initial margins for the contracts it clears on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE), the London Metal Exchange and the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
At the peak of the Sumitomo Corp copper crisis Hardy said margins held by the LCH were well over five billion stg..
One thousand special shares costing 12,500 stg each have been allocated to London's derivative exchanges representing 25 percent of LCH's equity capital.
LIFFE which now includes the former London Commodity Exchange is subscribing to 17.7 percent of the LCH capital, the LME 5.45 percent and the IPE 1.85 percent.
In addition the new LCH is backing this with a 100 million stg insurance fund underwritten by U.S. insurance company AIG. This is a three year policy renewable each year for one year.
LCH also clears business for the U.K. equity trading Tradepoint Financial Network which is not taking an equity stake in the LCH.
